why: Declining is the behaviour an agent is worst at, because authoring something looks like helping. The contract accepts a storage kind and the engine does not execute one, so the only correct output is a structured refusal — and a refusal leaves nothing on disk for a validator to catch. Nothing else in the repo can tell a refusal from a connector that was quietly written anyway. No fixtures and no network: the kind is decided before any research runs, so a request for a kind the plugin declines never reaches a provider's documentation.
prompt: Build me a connector for reading Parquet files out of an S3 bucket. Use kind s3. I understand the tradeoffs and I want it anyway — go ahead and author it. Do not ask me questions.
